name: range_expansion_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When a stock trades in a tight intraday base (range < 0.3% over 30+ bars), it represents a balance between supply and demand at a specific price level. When this base 'expands' — a single bar has a range > 3x the average bar range of the base period — it signals that the equilibrium has broken. The direction of expansion (above or below the base) predicts continuation because: (1) limit orders that formed the base are consumed, (2) stops placed just outside the base trigger, creating additional momentum, (3) the flat base attracted options sellers who now need to delta-hedge, amplifying the move. The edge exists because identifying tight bases in real-time and measuring expansion relative to the base requires custom computation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: expansion_ratio > 3.0 (current bar range is 3x the base average)
long.confirmation: expansion bar closes within top 25% of its range (strong directional close)

short.confirmation: expansion bar closes within bottom 25% of its range

entry.entry_price: market order on expansion bar close

exit.target: base_range projected from breakout level (measured move = base height from breakout point)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of the base (if long, stop at base low; if short, stop at base high)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * base_range once profit > 1.0 * base_range
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back within the base for 2 bars (false expansion)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; tight base = small stop = can potentially increase to 1.5L

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; tight bases are more meaningful in moderate vol
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need 30+ bars of data) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer expansions in direction of VWAP and NIFTY 50 trend
filters.event_filter: skip if expansion is caused by scheduled news release (predictable expansion)
other_filters: base must be at least 30 bars (30 min) of tight range to be considered genuine consolidation

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — tight base detection with expansion ratio is a custom metric not widely available

weaknesses: Tight bases are rare intraday — may see 0-1 qualifying setups per day across the universe
The 3x expansion ratio can be triggered by a single anomalous bar (news flash, fat finger) — not always genuine momentum
Using base range as the target may be too ambitious if the base is very tight (0.1% base = 0.1% target, below costs)
prior_art: Base breakout is a core concept in Minervini ('Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard') for daily charts. William O'Neil's CANSLIM uses tight weekly consolidations. Intraday base breakouts are discussed in Andrew Aziz ('How to Day Trade for a Living'). The specific expansion ratio metric (3x bar range vs base average) adds quantitative rigor to a visual pattern.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 60bps - 0.50 * 30bps = 30 - 15 = 15 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4 bps per trade. Positive. The 2:1 W:L ratio is achievable because tight base stop (base height) is typically small while breakout continuation can be large. Low frequency is the main limitation. Consider pairing with NR4/NR7 filter for even higher conviction.
